question: I have only Basic Autoplan and caused a crash in B.C. What coverage distinction matters before I assume my own car's repairs will be paid?
generated_answer:
In B.C., if you only have Basic Autoplan and you cause a crash, the coverage distinction that matters is whether you have collision coverage. Basic Autoplan typically includes third-party liability coverage, which pays for damages to others, but it may not cover damages to your own vehicle unless you have collision coverage.

If you don't have collision coverage, you'll likely be responsible for paying for the repairs to your own vehicle. However, if the other party involved in the crash is at fault, their insurance may cover the damages to your vehicle, but you'll need to work with their insurer to get the repairs done.

It's also important to note that if you're found to be at fault for the crash, you may also be responsible for paying for damages to the other party's vehicle, which would be covered by your third-party liability coverage.

To confirm your coverage and understand your responsibilities, it's best to contact your insurance provider and review your policy details. They can help you understand what's covered and what's not, and guide you through the process of getting your vehicle repaired.

Additionally, if you're concerned about being without collision coverage, you may want to consider adding it to your policy to protect yourself financially in case of a future crash. However, keep in mind that adding collision coverage will likely increase your premiums.

In summary, if you only have Basic Autoplan and cause a crash, you'll need to check if you have collision coverage to determine if your own vehicle's repairs will be paid. If not, you may be responsible for the repairs, but you can work with the other party's insurer if they're at fault. It's always best to review your policy and contact your insurer for clarification.
